Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — ACME discovery

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- TL;DR: ACME is evaluating an LLM inference platform to replace a self-hosted setup; priority is predictable 99th pct latency (<250ms for 512 tokens), throughput for batch scoring of ~200 qps, and strong audit logs.
- Open technical items: end-to-end p95/99 latency under your traffic shape, KV/prefix caching behavior for short-lived session loads, and model quantization tradeoffs for cost targets.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll share our internal latency/throughput benchmarks for a similar workload (attached).
2) Dev from our team can run a quick config suggestion and answer any kernel/quantization questions — can you confirm which instance types you plan to use for Dedicated?
3) If numbers look good, we can schedule a brief tech deep-dive with your infra/ML engineers next week.

Attached: acme_latency_report_v2.pdf (high-level numbers) and CSV with raw runs.

If priority has shifted, let me know — otherwise I'll follow up with the deeper numbers from Dev.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the fast follow-up. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we set the deep-dive: 

1) For latency, when you say 99th pct <250ms, is that cold-start inclusive or warm-only? Our traffic has a mix of short sessions and long-lived chats.
2) For throughput: 200 qps is peak for batch scoring — can you share p95/p99 at that sustained rate and the instance types you used?

We're on GCP N2 with A100s for proofs of concept but planning a Dedicated rollout. If you can surface the raw CSV we can forward to infra for quick review.

Thanks,
Alex
Sr ML Eng — ACME Corp
alex.chen@acme.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — ACME discovery

Hi Alex — thanks for the questions. Quick answers inline, and attached are the raw run CSVs referenced in Marissa's note.

- 99th pct: numbers in the PDF/CSV are warm steady-state (KV cache primed). Cold-starts depend heavily on model size and batch window; for your 512-token profile we typically see cold p99 ~350-500ms on A100 (single-request path) but warm p99 consistently <250ms with continuous traffic and prefix caching.
- Throughput: the CSV (redwood-latency-benchmarks-3-8-26.csv) contains runs at 50/100/200 qps sustained. At 200 qps on a 4xA100 pool with continuous batching we measured p95 ~95ms, p99 ~210-230ms for 512-token sequences.
- Instance types: these runs were 4xA100 (40GB) equivalent; we can provide configs for N2 with A100 and also lower-cost alternatives with quantized int8 builds.

Attached: redwood-latency-benchmarks-3-8-26.csv

If helpful I can also cook up a short test run using your N2/A100 configuration — would you be able to share a sample sequence length distribution and a small tokenized sample?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
